name: NullClaw
vibe_summary: A hyper-minimalist OpenClaw-compatible agent runtime written in pure Zig, shipping as a 678 KB static binary with ~1 MB RAM usage and sub-2ms boot. It aims to be the smallest fully autonomous AI assistant infrastructure that runs on literally anything with a CPU.
best_for: Running agents on $5 SBCs and constrained edge hardware
Users who want a single static binary with zero runtime dependencies
Tinkerers who value portability across ARM, x86, and RISC-V
avoid_if: You want a mature GUI/dashboard experience out of the box
You need a large established plugin ecosystem and community
You prefer mainstream languages with bigger contributor pools
You need battle-tested production stability at scale
openclaw_advantages: Dramatically smaller footprint: 678 KB binary and ~1 MB RAM vs OpenClaw's much heavier stack
Sub-2ms cold start, orders of magnitude faster boot
Single static binary runs on any CPU architecture with only libc
Multi-layer sandboxing (landlock, firejail, bubblewrap, docker) built in by design
50+ providers, 19 channels, and 10 memory engines in a tiny package
openclaw_disadvantages: Far smaller community and ecosystem (8k vs 300k+ stars)
Zig codebase means fewer potential contributors and less tooling maturity
UI layer (nullhub) is still in beta; OpenClaw has a polished Control UI
Less real-world production validation and third-party skill registry
Younger project with higher risk of breaking changes

overview_markdown:
NullClaw is a ground-up reimagining of OpenClaw-style autonomous AI assistant infrastructure written entirely in Zig. Its headline achievement is extreme minimalism: a 678 KB static binary with roughly 1 MB peak RSS that boots in under 2 ms on Apple Silicon and under 8 ms on a 0.8 GHz edge core, requiring nothing but libc. Despite the tiny footprint, it claims a feature-complete stack — 50+ LLM providers, 19 messaging channels, 35+ tools, 10 memory engines, tunnels, hardware peripherals, MCP support, subagents, streaming, and voice.

Architecturally, NullClaw leans on Zig's compile-time guarantees: no garbage collector, no runtime, no allocator overhead, and core systems (providers, channels, tools, memory, tunnels, peripherals) exposed as swappable vtable interfaces. Security is a stated design pillar, with pairing, multi-layer sandboxing via landlock, firejail, bubblewrap, or Docker, explicit allowlists, workspace scoping, and encrypted secrets. Recent commits show active hardening work — stderr isolation for agent runners, allocation-free gateway bind paths, and config validation that fails closed rather than silently dropping messages.

Compared to OpenClaw, NullClaw trades ecosystem maturity for radical efficiency and portability. It targets the opposite end of the spectrum: $5 ARM boards, RISC-V experiments, and environments where OpenClaw's heavier Node-based stack simply won't fit. The surrounding Null ecosystem (nullhub UI, nullboiler orchestration, nullwatch observability, nulltickets task tracking) is emerging but still in beta, so users should expect a more DIY experience than OpenClaw's polished dashboard and massive skills registry.
